params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The lavender cloud creature springs straight up onto the coffee counter in one hard leap and hammers both stubby arms across the counter top in a typing blur, its whole body bouncing on every hit, while the lines of code on the big screen above it scroll upward faster and faster. It stops, tips its head back and peers up at the screen, then throws both arms overhead in triumph and hops on the spot. It drops back down to the floor, lands square, and springs straight back up onto the counter to hammer again, faster.

The big screen stays lit and full of dense lines of code in every frame, and the lines scroll upward without pause. Its face is exactly one pale chevron and one short straight bar, the same chevron and the same bar in every frame. It lands on both feet after every leap. It stays small, no taller than a quarter of the black server rack beside it, in every frame. The server rack, the coffee machine, the jug, the mugs, the water cooler and the doorway stay the same drawings in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
